title: Mark Villar seeks hazard pay, extra insurance for media workers deployed to dangerous assignments
summary: Senator Mark Villar is pushing for additional protection for media workers who are deployed to hazardous locations, filing a measure that would provide them with hazard pay and expanded insurance…

blocks.text: Senator Mark Villar is pushing for additional protection for media workers who are deployed to hazardous locations, filing a measure that would provide them with hazard pay and expanded insurance coverage while carrying out dangerous assignments. Villar filed Senate Bill No. 2440, or the proposed “Media Workers Hazard Pay Act,” which seeks to provide financial and insurance benefits to accredited media personnel assigned to areas affected by armed conflict, disasters, disease outbreaks, and other emergency situations. “Media workers serve as the eyes and ears of the public during the most difficult and dangerous situations. Kung inaasahan natin silang humarap sa panganib upang mapanatiling ligtas at may sapat na kaalaman ang ating mga kababayan, tungkulin din nating tiyakin na sila ay protektado, insured, at makatarungang binabayaran,” Villar said. The senator pointed to previous incidents involving journalists who encountered serious risks while performing their duties. Among them was a television reporter who spent nearly two weeks in the hospital in 2022 after contracting leptospirosis while covering an incident in Payatas, Quezon City. Another reporter assigned to provide weather updates in 2024 also found himself affected by flooding in his own community and struggled to protect his belongings. Under Villar's proposal, accredited media workers from both government and private-sector organizations would qualify for a minimum hazard pay of ₱650 per day when their duties require them to physically report from dangerous areas. These would include conflict-affected or embattled locations, isolated or distressed stations, areas affected by infectious diseases, and places placed under a state of calamity or emergency. The additional pay would cover the entire period of the hazardous assignment and could not be lowered. However, employees who already receive hazard compensation equal to or greater than the proposed amount would not receive a separate benefit under the measure. The bill would also compel employers to provide additional insurance protection to covered media workers. The proposed package includes a ₱200,000 death benefit for those who die while performing their duties, as well as disability compensation of up to ₱200,000 for total or partial disability caused by injuries sustained in the line of duty. Medical insurance coverage of up to ₱100,000 would also be provided to each covered worker. Villar's proposal further seeks additional compensation for media personnel required to work beyond the standard eight-hour shift or during the 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. period, subject to existing laws and accepted industry practices. The senator said the benefits are necessary given the risks routinely faced by journalists and other media personnel, including reporters, camera operators, and technical staff, particularly when covering disasters and other emergencies. According to Villar, media workers play an important role in delivering verified information, government warnings, disaster preparedness instructions, and emergency contact numbers to communities during crises. “Behind every live report from a flooded community, conflict area, or disease-infested location is a media worker who chooses to fulfill his or her duty despite the risks. Their courage and public service must be recognized through concrete and enforceable benefits,” Villar said.
